# Brave Bunnies

"Brave Bunnies" is a Ukrainian animated preschool television series that follows the adventures of two bunny siblings, Bop and Boo, as they travel the world with their family aboard the "Bunny Bus" , . Created by Olga Cherepanova, the series is designed for children aged two to five and aims to teach social-emotional learning through playful storytelling , . The show promotes themes of diversity, acceptance, curiosity, creativity, and courage , . It is a 2D-animated series comprising 104 seven-minute episodes across two seasons , . Its development history is uniquely intertwined with geopolitical events, particularly the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, which led to a significant restructuring of its production and ownership, with Canadian media company WildBrain acquiring majority control to ensure the franchise's continuity , . The series premiered globally on December 5, 2020, and has since been broadcast in over 80 countries worldwide , .

## Premise and Characters

The central premise of "Brave Bunnies" revolves around a family of curious and courageous bunnies who embark on a "Big Journey" to explore the world and discover new friends across diverse biomes such as jungles, savannahs, forests, plains, and mountains , . The primary vehicles for this exploration are the "Bunny Bus," a mobile home for the rabbit family, and the "Bunny Bike," a smaller mode of transport used for more intimate adventures , . The narrative structure of each episode is consistent, focusing on the siblings Bop and Boo meeting animal children who live in the various environments they visit . These encounters often involve playing games and engaging in activities that foster friendship and celebrate differences , . The overarching goal of the series is to model positive behaviors and provide young viewers with real-life strategies for communicating across differences without fear or stereotypes, thereby promoting values such as respect for global diversity, empathy, and problem-solving , . The show is explicitly educational, aiming to teach preschoolers about acceptance of diversity, communication with peers who are different, and essential social interaction skills through its episodic format . This educational mandate is reinforced by the involvement of child psychologists in the script development process to ensure the content effectively fosters empathy, acceptance, and respect for diversity .

The main cast of characters forms the heart of the series. The titular protagonists are Bop and Boo, brother and sister bunnies who lead the explorations , . They embody the series' core value of "bunny bravery," demonstrating curiosity, creativity, openness, responsibility, and an eagerness to learn and experience new things , . Their parents, Ma Bunny and Pa Bunny, accompany them on their journeys, providing guidance and support . The family also includes four younger siblings known as the Bunny Babies, who add to the dynamic and familial feel of the show , . Beyond the immediate family, the bunnies encounter a wide array of animal friends throughout their travels. These include a tiger, kangaroo, bear, fox, and llama, among others, representing the diverse wildlife and cultures they discover . The series also features recurring non-bunny characters such as Ricky Racoon and Franny Fox, who appear in the book adaptations and help reinforce the themes of friendship and cooperation . Each character is designed to contribute to the show's mission of promoting inclusivity and positive social interactions. The visual style of the series is bright and kid-friendly, complementing its cheerful and adventurous tone . The combination of social skill-building, educational content, comedy, catchy songs, and a vibrant aesthetic creates an engaging and accessible experience for its target preschool audience .

## Development and Production History

The creation of "Brave Bunnies" originated from the creative vision of Olga Cherepanova, a Ukrainian creative producer and author who conceived the original story , . She co-founded the Ukrainian studio Glowberry Creative Production, which was established in 2009 as a niche publishing house before evolving into a dynamic international creative and production company focused on developing children's animated content , . Glowberry became part of FILM.UA Group in 2016 , . The series was developed at Glowberry under the leadership of Olga Cherepanova, who served as the Creative Director and series creator , . The production team assembled for the series reflected a deliberate strategy to create a globally appealing property from its inception. The creative team included UK-based director Tim Fehrenbach, Canadian head writer John van Bruggen, and Ukrainian art director Anna Sarvira , , . This multinational collaboration was instrumental in shaping the show's international appeal and facilitating its co-production and distribution deals. The series received official support from the Ukrainian State Film Agency and the Ministry of Culture of Ukraine, highlighting its significance within the national creative industry , .

The initial production phase of "Brave Bunnies" was a co-production between the Ukrainian studio Glowberry and the Spanish animation studio Ánima Kitchent , , . Globally, the series was distributed by the multi-award-winning UK-based studio Aardman Animations, a partnership brokered by the content agency Big Picture Licensing (BPL) , , . The series was pitched at MIPJunior 2020 and attracted the highest number of viewers in the Screening Library, signaling strong international interest from the outset . Season 1 consisted of 52 episodes, each seven minutes long , . The production process for Season 1 was marked by adaptability; voice recording sessions were handled by Fitzrovia Post in London and were adapted for remote work using Covid-safe technology under the direction of Keiran Brown, showcasing the industry's resilience during the pandemic .

The most significant turning point in the franchise's history occurred in February 2022 with the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine . The conflict caused the production of "Brave Bunnies" to be suspended, placing the future of the intellectual property in jeopardy . In response to this disruption, a pivotal corporate restructuring took place. In December 2022, Canadian media giant WildBrain acquired a majority stake in the "Brave Bunnies" IP through a three-way partnership facilitated by Big Picture Licensing , , . Under this agreement, WildBrain became the majority stakeholder, while Glowberry and Ánima retained minority stakes , . This acquisition allowed WildBrain to assume global co-production, distribution, licensing, and merchandising leadership for all future seasons, effectively stepping in to secure the franchise's continuity . The production of Season 2 resumed with WildBrain's Vancouver animation studio joining Glowberry and Ánima as a co-producer , . Season 2, also consisting of 52 seven-minute episodes, was delivered beginning in June 2023 , , . This strategic intervention by WildBrain not only stabilized the project but also ensured its continued growth on the global stage, transforming the ownership and management structure of the beloved franchise .

## Broadcast and Distribution

Since its debut, "Brave Bunnies" has achieved significant international success, securing broadcast rights in over 80 countries worldwide , . The series began its journey with a premiere on the PLUSPLUS TV channel in Ukraine on December 5, 2020 , . Following its domestic launch, it quickly expanded its global footprint, premiering in the United Kingdom on Milkshake! (Channel 5) on February 6, 2021 , . This UK premiere was notably successful, reaching a total audience of 4.4 million and ranking #1 in its commercial channel time slots . Other early international premieres occurred in Germany on Super RTL in March 2021, Israel on HOP! in April 2021, and Australia on ABC in September 2021 , . The series has maintained a steady expansion into new territories, with broadcasts launching in Norway, Sweden, Finland, and Latvia in 2021 . By October 2021, the series had already secured broadcast in a dozen countries, including South Korea and Canada .

The distribution network for "Brave Bunnies" is extensive and includes both linear television and digital streaming platforms across multiple continents. Key broadcasters have acquired the series for their pre-school programming blocks, including Nick Jr. in the UK, Family Jr. in Canada, Super RTL in Germany, Yle in Finland, and HOP! in Israel . A major milestone in its distribution was the acquisition by HBO Max for Latin America (LATAM), where it premiered in mid-2022 , . Subsequently, WarnerMedia secured a licensing deal for the series to air in 20 territories across Southeast Asia, Australia, and New Zealand, premiering on the Cartoonito block on Cartoon Network in Southeast Asia and on HBO GO in Taiwan and Hong Kong . The series continued its European expansion in 2024, launching in Norway, Germany, the UK, and Sweden . In Poland, Season 2 is set to launch on TeleTOON+ , . As of late 2025, the series remains widely available on various platforms. It can be streamed ad-free on Sunflower TV's YouTube channel for Ukrainian refugees , and is available on general SVOD services like Hoopla in the United States and Canada, Paramount+ in the United Kingdom, and Foxtel Now in Australia . However, there appears to be a discrepancy in the availability of Season 2; while its first episode aired on November 30, 2023, it remained unavailable for streaming or rental on any service as of that date, indicating potential logistical or contractual challenges in its rollout .

## Multimedia Expansion

The "Brave Bunnies" franchise has successfully expanded beyond its original television series into a robust multimedia ecosystem, encompassing a book series and a line of licensed consumer products. This diversification strategy has helped to build brand recognition and extend engagement with its preschool audience across multiple platforms. The book series adaptation began with a collection launched in Italy in Q4 2021, published by DeA Planeta Libri, a subsidiary of Grupo Planeta and DeAgostini , . This initial Italian release included sticker books titled *Amici Incredibili* (Incredible Friends) and *In Giro per il Mondo* (Around the World), alongside hardcover titles such as *Eroi Controvento* (Brave Heroes), *Strisce da Esploratore* (Hidden Treasure), and *Pulizia Cosmica* (A Great Mess) , . The books were distributed nationally through 800 bookstores, online platforms, and over 300 mass-market outlets , . The franchise's literary presence continued to grow with the acquisition of publishing rights by Ladybird, an imprint of Penguin Random House, in the United Kingdom . Ladybird released its first two books, *Brave Bunnies Spring to the Rescue* and *Brave Bunnies Make a Friend*, in March 2022 . In Australia, Five Mile Publishing holds the publishing rights, and in the UK, the first book in the series, *Brave Bunnies in the Jungle*, was authored by Olga Cherepanova and illustrated by Anna Sarvira, with development input from child psychologist Natalia Pashko, further emphasizing the franchise's educational focus , . The books feature the same core characters, including Bop, Boo, Ma Bunny, Ricky Racoon, and Franny Fox, and continue to promote social-emotional learning themes like bravery, playfulness, and friendship .

The expansion into consumer products is centered around a strategic partnership with Spin Master, who serves as the global master toy licensee for the "Brave Bunnies" intellectual property , . Spin Master launched the first range of licensed toys in spring 2022 and followed up with a significant product launch in Germany and Italy in the third quarter of 2023 , . The toy line includes a variety of products such as figures, plush toys, playsets, games, and puzzles, all designed to align with the series' spirit of exploration and adventure , . A key aspect of this product launch was its innovative and environmentally conscious packaging. The packaging is plastic-free and designed for dual use, featuring reusable cardboard punch-out props and coloring sheets that integrate directly into the play experience , . This design choice reflects modern sustainability trends and reinforces the brand's positive values. The products were made available at major retailers in both countries, including Toys Center, Prenatal, and IBS in Italy, and Smyths, Mueller, and MyToys in Germany , . The timing of this launch in mid-2023 was particularly significant, occurring during the ongoing war in Ukraine . Olga Cherepanova publicly expressed that the launch provided "assurance that together we can bring back a prosperous time for all," framing it as a symbol of hope and resilience , . James Martin, Senior Vice President of Marketing at Spin Master, confirmed that the company's management of the "Brave Bunnies" toy line remains active and continues to be a key part of its Entertainment content pipeline, as cited in multiple 2024 financial results presentations , , , .

## Business Ecosystem and Ownership

The business ecosystem surrounding "Brave Bunnies" is characterized by a complex co-production and rights management structure that evolved significantly following the Russian invasion of Ukraine. Initially, the intellectual property (IP) was owned and developed by Glowberry, the Ukrainian studio founded by creator Olga Cherepanova , . Production for Season 1 was a co-production between Glowberry and the Spanish studio Ánima Kitchent , . Global distribution and licensing for Season 1 were managed by the UK-based studio Aardman Animations, a move facilitated by the content agency Big Picture Licensing (BPL) , . This initial setup positioned the franchise for immediate international distribution upon its release. However, the full-scale Russian invasion in February 2022 forced the suspension of production and triggered a fundamental shift in the franchise's corporate ownership and operational control , .

In December 2022, a pivotal transaction saw Canadian media conglomerate WildBrain acquire a majority stake in the "Brave Bunnies" IP , . This acquisition was formalized through a three-way partnership between WildBrain, Glowberry, and Ánima, again facilitated by Big Picture Licensing , . As part of this agreement, WildBrain assumed the role of majority stakeholder, taking over global co-production, distribution, licensing, and merchandising responsibilities for Season 2 onwards , . The production of Season 2, which was delivered beginning in June 2023, was co-produced by WildBrain’s Vancouver animation studio alongside Glowberry and Ánima, the original producers of Season 1 , , . While WildBrain now leads the global management of the franchise, the original creators and partners retain significant interests and territorial rights. Specifically, Glowberry retains distribution and licensing rights within Ukraine, and Ánima retains these rights in Spain , . This territorial rights model allows the original stakeholders to maintain a presence and control in their respective home markets. WildBrain CPLG, the licensing arm of WildBrain, manages global distribution and consumer products, ensuring a cohesive global strategy , .

The commercialization of the franchise is managed through a network of specialized partners. The global master toy license is held by Spin Master, who has been actively managing the "Brave Bunnies" toy line as part of its Entertainment content pipeline , . Spin Master's continued reporting on the franchise in its 2024 financial results confirms its ongoing relevance and commercial activity , . For publishing, rights are handled by different partners in various regions: KidsMe serves as the exclusive distributor and licensing agent in Italy, Ladybird (an imprint of Penguin Random House) in the UK, and Five Mile Publishing in Australia , , . This decentralized yet coordinated approach to rights management allows the franchise to be effectively localized and marketed in key territories while being overseen by a single global entity, WildBrain, for strategic direction and large-scale operations. This structure balances the need for global consistency with the importance of local market expertise.

## Reception and Significance

"Brave Bunnies" has been generally well-received for its positive messaging and educational content tailored to a preschool audience. Parental feedback highlights that the series effectively models desirable social behaviors, such as sharing toys, helping friends, and apologizing when necessary . The show is noted for its gentle handling of emotional moments, such as disappointment or fear, resolving them quickly and constructively . It delivers a clear moral at the end of each episode, reinforcing themes like the value of friendship or the joy of discovery . Critics and reviewers have praised its focus on fostering empathy, acceptance, and respect for diversity, with some noting the intentional involvement of child psychologists in the script development process to achieve these goals . The series is categorized as an entertaining and educational 2D animated program that successfully combines social skill-building with comedy, catchy songs, and a bright visual style to engage its young viewers , . The show's emphasis on themes like curiosity, creativity, teamwork, and kindness aligns with contemporary expectations for high-quality preschool programming , . Some parental reviews suggest that while the resolution of conflicts is effective, the show may occasionally oversimplify emotional challenges, though this is a common characteristic of the genre .

Beyond its critical reception, "Brave Bunnies" holds profound symbolic significance, particularly due to its origins in Ukraine and the circumstances surrounding its production. The franchise was born out of the Ukrainian creative industry and represents a significant achievement for the sector, described by its creator as a "huge breakthrough for the Ukrainian animation world" . This national pride was amplified by the events of the full-scale Russian invasion in February 2022. The subsequent acquisition of the majority IP by WildBrain was framed not just as a commercial decision but as an act of corporate solidarity that ensured the survival of a culturally important Ukrainian asset , . The launch of the Spin Master toy line in Germany and Italy in mid-2023, timed with the ongoing war, was imbued with powerful symbolism. Olga Cherepanova publicly stated that the launch provided "assurance that together we can bring back a prosperous time for all," positioning the franchise as a beacon of hope, resilience, and collective optimism , . This narrative transforms the product launch from a purely commercial event into a culturally resonant one, connecting the brand directly to the experiences and aspirations of Ukrainians during a time of crisis. The franchise thus serves as a case study in how creative industries can demonstrate resilience and how brands can navigate and leverage geopolitical events to connect with audiences on a deeper, more human level.

The "Brave Bunnies" multimedia ecosystem encompasses a book series and a line of licensed consumer products.
The diversification strategy of "Brave Bunnies" has helped to build brand recognition.
The diversification strategy of "Brave Bunnies" has helped to extend engagement with its preschool audience across multiple platforms.

DeA Planeta Libri is a subsidiary of Grupo Planeta and DeAgostini.

Ukrainian-Produced ‘Brave Bunnies’ Returns with Season 2 in 2023
================================================================

New Wildbrain, Glowberry and Ánimas’ agreement ensures the continued production of the popular preschool animated series despite its disruption caused by the Russian invasion of Ukraine.

By [Debbie Diamond Sarto](https://www.awn.com/users/debbie-diamond-sarto "View Debbie Diamond Sarto's profile.") | Monday, December 5, 2022 at 10:13am

In [2D](https://www.awn.com/2d), [Business](https://www.awn.com/business), [CG](https://www.awn.com/cg), [Licensing](https://www.awn.com/licensing), [People](https://www.awn.com/people), [Television](https://www.awn.com/television) | [ANIMATIONWorld](https://www.awn.com/animationworld), [Headline News](https://www.awn.com/news) | Geographic Region: [All](https://www.awn.com/regions/all)

[![Image 3](https://www.awn.com/sites/default/files/styles/inline/public/image/featured/bbf_kangaroo_and_bunnies-1280.jpg?itok=zAstanlc)](https://www.awn.com/sites/default/files/styles/original/public/image/featured/bbf_kangaroo_and_bunnies-1280.jpg?itok=KrovKEoH)

WildBrain has partnered with Ukrainian-based Glowberry to bring the _Brave Bunnies_ preschool brand into its kids’ and family franchise portfolio. Under the arrangement, WildBrain has assured the continuation of the popular series disrupted by the Russian invasion of Ukraine. Working with Glowberry and the Ibero-American animation studio, Ánima, WildBrain will lead global management of the franchise, leveraging its 360° capabilities across production, distribution, and consumer products. Glowberry co-founder Olga Cherepanova created _Brave Bunnies_ and is the series’ creative director.

_Brave Bunnies_ Season 2 will be co-produced by WIldbrain’s Vancouver studio, with delivery expected in June 2023. WildBrain CPLG, the company’s dedicated consumer products agency, will manage licensing and merchandising worldwide. In addition, the company’s own Family Jr. channel has picked up _Brave Bunnies_ Season 1 (produced by Glowberry and Ánima) for exclusive linear telecast in Canada. Glowberry retains distribution and licensing rights for the brand in Ukraine, while Ánima has distribution rights in Spain. The three-way partnership, which Big Picture Licensing facilitated, sees WildBrain become the majority stakeholder in the _Brave Bunnies_ IP, with Glowberry and Ánima as minority stakeholders.

“_Brave Bunnies_ is a kids’ property born of tremendous creative vision and has the potential to be a major preschool franchise, having already established a solid foundation with audiences through compelling content and consumer products,” commented Wildbrain CEO Eric Ellenbogen. “Following the terrible events in Ukraine this year, we saw it as vital to ensure the future of this wonderful property, and we couldn’t be more pleased now to be collaborating with Olga Cherepanova and her Glowberry team, along with the creative team at Ánima, on the next big adventures for the _Brave Bunnies_.”

The 2D-animated series for kids ages 2-5 follows the adventures of two curious and inspiring bunny siblings—Boo and Bop—who create joy and excitement in their lives by bravely seeking out new friends, games, and experiences. The series fosters curiosity, creativity, eagerness, openness, and responsibility while encouraging kids to ask, “What if...?”

[![Image 4](https://www.awn.com/sites/default/files/styles/inline/public/image/attached/1058727-bbfmooseandbunnies-1280.jpg?itok=KSct9Iqx)](https://www.awn.com/sites/default/files/styles/original/public/image/attached/1058727-bbfmooseandbunnies-1280.jpg?itok=o88KehpQ)

“I created _Brave Bunnies_ to help children all over the world communicate with different friends without any fears or stereotypes, respecting the diversity of our world,” shared Cherepanova. “Each episode of _Brave Bunnies_ shows real-life examples of how to find a unique approach to each person without pressure or changing anyone’s uniqueness. This idea is essential for healthy childhood development.”

Adding, “Unfortunately, after the Russian invasion of Ukraine, the Glowberry team faced significant challenges. Many employees were forced to flee Kyiv because of personal safety and the lives of their loved ones. But thanks to the support of partners like WildBrain and Ánima, now we have the opportunity to continue to create and share _Brave Bunnies_ together.”

“I’m proud and happy that this project born in Ukraine will now continue to spread around the world, helping the next generation develop respect for diversity and build relationships based on co-creation and cooperation rather than on fear and violence,” concluded Cherepanova. “On behalf of the Ukrainian team, I want to express my deep gratitude to all the partners and talented people working together on Brave Bunnies, who have done so much despite the challenges we all faced. We do hope for peace in Ukraine and will do everything possible for a peaceful tomorrow.”

“From Ánima, we want to thank both WildBrain and Glowberry,” said Ánima, Spain CEO Ángel Molinero. “We are very excited about the future of the project, and we believe WildBrain is the perfect partner to give continuity to the Brave Bunnies brand.”

_Brave Bunnies_ Season 1 is on kids' platforms in more than 80 countries across LatAm, Canada, the UK, Europe, Nordics, the Middle East, Asia, and Australia. A complimentary toy line for _Brave Bunnies_ was launched by kids’ entertainment company Spin Master in Germany and Italy earlier this year. In addition, the franchise’s first books have debuted in Italy from publisher Planeta Libre, an imprint of De Agostini, who are also co-producers of the animated series; in Australia from Five Mile Publishing; and in the UK from Ladybird, an imprint of Penguin Random House.

In season one of _Brave Bunnies_ (52 x 7’), Boo and Bop are on a big adventure in the Bunny Bus with Ma and Pa and their four wee siblings, the Bunny Babies. Together, they bravely explore the Bunny World, traveling to the jungle, savannah, forest, plains, and mountains. Along the way, Boo and Bop meet new animal children, including a tiger, kangaroo, bear, fox, and llama. Despite their differences, they always find a way to make friends and play new games!

For season two (52 x 7’), the _Brave Bunnies_ continue their road trip adventure around the Bunny World, encountering a few old friends and making more new ones! In this season, Boo and Bop have some big surprises in store for small viewers as they visit their “Best Bunny Friends” at their homes, meet their families, explore their unique lifestyles, and find new adventures.

_Source: WIldbrain_

Spin Master and Glowberry Debut BRAVE BUNNIES Toys in Italy and Germany
=======================================================================

Posted by [Rebecca Ash](https://www.totallicensing.com/author/rebecca-ash/ "Posts by Rebecca Ash") | Apr 11, 2022 | [News](https://www.totallicensing.com/category/news/), [Top news story](https://www.totallicensing.com/category/top-news-story/) |

![Image 15: Spin Master and Glowberry Debut BRAVE BUNNIES Toys in Italy and Germany](https://www.totallicensing.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/Screenshot-2022-04-11-at-14.32.34-1280x640.png)

Spin Master Corp., master toy licensee for Ukrainian creative production company Glowberry’s _BRAVE BUNNIES_ series, has announced today the launch of _BRAVE BUNNIES_ toys in Italy and Germany. The toy line includes an assortment of playsets, figures, plush, games and puzzles.

Aimed at preschoolers and based on an original idea by Olga Cherepanova, _BRAVE BUNNIES_ is co-created with Spanish animation studio Ánima and is distributed internationally by Aardman. The _BRAVE BUNNIES_ series follows the story of the curious and courageous _BRAVE BUNNIES_ family as they go on a BIG Journey to explore the diverse world around them and find new friends. With a focus on helping children with their first socialization through various games, the series teaches kids to accept differences and be courageous in exploring the world around them.

“_BRAVE BUNNIES_ encourages preschoolers to explore the world around them and this same spirit applies to the toy line,” said James Martin, Spin Master’s SVP of Marketing & Global Brand Team Lead, Preschool. “We’ve thoughtfully designed the plastic-free packaging to give it a second life as part of the play experience, including artful cardboard punch-out props and coloring sheets. We can’t wait for preschoolers to unbox, explore and bring the caring characters and their adventures to life through play.”

“The launch of the _BRAVE BUNNIES_ toy line marks a significant milestone for the whole international team,” said [Olga Cherepanova](https://www.linkedin.com/in/olga-cherepanova-814579147/?originalSubdomain=ua), the author of the original idea and creative producer of _BRAVE BUNNIES__. **“**_During this painful time for all Ukrainians, the toy launch gives us assurance that together we can bring back a prosperous time for all. We sincerely hope that the toys will bring joy and happiness to kids around the world and pave the way to safe and exciting experiences. We are very grateful to Spin Master for their continued support on _BRAVE BUNNIES_.”

_BRAVE BUNNIES_ toys are now available at Toys Center, Prenatal and IBS, along with mass retailers’ e-commerce websites in Italy. The toy line is also launching this month at Smyths, Mueller and MyToys in Germany.

First launched in 2020,  _BRAVE BUNNIES_ is broadcast in 63 countries around the world. Recently the show extended its reach by landing in Latin America and the Caribbean on HBO Max and Pan-South-East Asia and Australia on the Cartoonito block on Cartoon Network.

_**Brave Bunnies**_ ([Ukrainian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukrainian_language "Ukrainian language"): Хоробрі зайці, [romanized](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romanization_of_Ukrainian "Romanization of Ukrainian"): _Khorobri zaitsi_) is a [Ukrainian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Television_in_Ukraine "Television in Ukraine") [children's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Children%27s_television_series "Children's television series") [animated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animated_series "Animated series") television series for [preschool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Preschool "Preschool") children aged 2 to 5. In the series, two rabbit children show their courage when they meet and befriend other animals. Creator Olga Cherepanova sought to encourage respect for diversity and to promote healthy childhood development.

The series has been broadcast in more than 80 countries. The first season was produced by Glowberry and [Ánima Kitchent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%81nima_/(company/) "Ánima (company)") in partnership with distributor [Aardman Animations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aardman_Animations "Aardman Animations"), and premiered in December 2020. Production of the second season was interrupted by the [Russian invasion of Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine "Russian invasion of Ukraine"), and resumed in December 2022 after [WildBrain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WildBrain "WildBrain") acquired a majority ownership of the property. A second season was distributed by WildBrain in 2023.

The 2D animated series follows the adventures of a family of rabbits:[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-MilliganGlowberry-1) Boo and Bop, Ma and Pa, and four Bunny Babies.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-SartoBunnies-2) Every episode starts with a cheerful song as the family ride on their bunny bus, which stops at a new location. Brother Bop and sister Boo then explore and make friends with a different animal, creating a new game to play with them. The series attempts to show its preschool viewers the diversity of the world and to accept the differences of others.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-MilliganGlowberry-1) Starting in the second season, some episodes have the bunny family revisit friends at their homes, meeting their families and learning more about their different lifestyles.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-MilliganWildBrain-3)

The series introduces children to the concept of diversity and, through the example of the Brave Bunnies, shows how to accept and communicate with people possessing different appearances and behaviours.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-TVguide-4)[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-MilliganGlowberry-1) To promote healthy childhood development, characters Bop and Boo acknowledge the uniqueness of each new friend.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-WildbrainPrimary3-5)

The Ukrainian voice cast includes actress [Olena Kravets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olena_Kravets "Olena Kravets") and singer-songwriter [Potap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Potap "Potap"), which [1+1 Media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1%2B1_Media "1+1 Media") stated was the first time a Ukrainian children's animated series attracted such high-profile performers.[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-1+1Cast-6)

*   Narrator – Chetna Pandya (English dub)[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-TVguideCast-7)
*   Bop – Wilbur Conabeare (English dub)[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-TVguideCast-7)
*   Boo – Margot Powell (English dub)[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-TVguideCast-7)
*   Bunny Ma – [Olena Kravets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olena_Kravets "Olena Kravets") (Ukrainian),[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-1+1Cast-6) Harriet Kershaw (English dub)[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-TVguideCast-7)
*   Bunny Pa – [Potap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Potap "Potap") (Ukrainian),[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-1+1Cast-6) Jensen Adeyanju (English dub)[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-TVguideCast-7)

Development and production
--------------------------

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Brave_Bunnies&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Development and production")\]

Publishing house Glowberry was founded in 2009 and worked in children's literature and illustration,[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-PrimaryGlowberry-8)[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-FilmUA-9) seeking to create modern fairy tales. Their best-selling work was a picture book about a family of rabbits on a journey, meeting unusual animals as they travelled further from their home. Several years were spent developing this into a television series[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-TyutyunenkoInterview-10) for children aged 2 to 5.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-MilliganWildBrain-3) Glowberry co-founder and series creator Olga Cherepanova[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-YossmanWildbrain-11)[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-Telekritika-12) noted that while rabbits are often considered to be timid animals, their bravery in the series comes from discovering new challenges every day.[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-TyutyunenkoInterview-10) She said that she created the series "to help children ... communicate with different friends without any fears or stereotypes, respecting the diversity of our world."[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-MilliganWildBrain-3)[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-SartoBunnies-2)

Illustrator Anna Sarvira[\[a\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-13) developed the style for the series, serving as art director while Cherepanova was the creative producer.[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-Telekritika-12) Following this early creative work, the production became an international project to ensure funding, market access, and expertise. Over a hundred people in different countries were involved, coordinating together on the same schedule.[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-TyutyunenkoInterview-10) This included British director Tim Fehrenbach and Canadian lead writer John Van Bruggen, both of whom had experience in children's animation.[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-Telekritika-12) Cherepanova was educated in psychology, and the writing team consulted with [child psychologists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Developmental_psychology "Developmental psychology") throughout the process. They sought to maintain the interest of young children, present stories that would aid [early socialisation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primary_socialization "Primary socialization"), and create characters representing the many different human [personality types](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Personality_type "Personality type").[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-Telekritika-12)[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-TyutyunenkoInterview-10) The music which celebrates the characters' achievements in each episode was composed in Ukraine.[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-NVfacts-14)

In 2019, the series was in development with Glowberry and Ánima Kitchent (the Spanish subsidiary of Mexico-based animation studio [Ánima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%81nima_/(company/) "Ánima (company)")).[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-PulidoAnima-15) The production also received support from the [Ukrainian State Film Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukrainian_State_Film_Agency "Ukrainian State Film Agency") and the [Ministry of Youth and Sports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Youth_and_Sports_/(Ukraine/) "Ministry of Youth and Sports (Ukraine)").[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-UkrinformItaly-16) Glowberry pitched the series to studios and distributors at [MIPCOM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MIPCOM "MIPCOM") in 2019. By early 2020, UK studio [Aardman Animations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aardman_Animations "Aardman Animations") had partnered as the international distributor and secured additional international sales at the 2020 [Kidscreen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidscreen "Kidscreen") Summit in Miami.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-MilliganGlowberry-1) The first season consisted of 52 seven-minute episodes.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-MilliganGlowberry-1)

When the full-scale [Russian invasion of Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine "Russian invasion of Ukraine") began in February 2022, the production of _Brave Bunnies_ in Kyiv was suspended.[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-YermakReporter-17) Many of the Glowberry team were forced to flee Kyiv,[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-YossmanWildbrain-11) and production coordinator Natalia Yermak became a war correspondent for the _[New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Times "New York Times")_.[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-YermakReporter-17) Production resumed in August[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-TyutyunenkoInterview-10) and by December 2022, Canadian children's entertainment company [WildBrain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WildBrain "WildBrain") became a majority stakeholder in _Brave Bunnies_, to continue the reliable production and distribution of the series.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-YossmanWildbrain-11) WildBrain took over global distribution of the series, merchandising and licensing, and the company's Vancouver animation studio joined Glowberry and Ánima Kitchent[\[b\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-20) to produce the second season of 52 episodes.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-YossmanWildbrain-11)[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-TownsendWildbrain-21)

The series premiered on 5 December 2020 on [PLUSPLUS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PLUSPLUS "PLUSPLUS") in Ukraine, followed by [Nick Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Jr. "Nick Jr.") (UK), [Super RTL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_RTL "Super RTL") (Germany), [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_Television_/(Australian_TV_network/) "ABC Television (Australian TV network)") (Australia), [Yle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yle "Yle") (Finland), and [HOP!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hop!_Channel "Hop! Channel") (Israel).[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-Telekritika-12) The first season was distributed by Aardman Animations,[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-MilliganGlowberry-1) and by 2022 had been broadcast in over 80 countries.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-MilliganWildBrain-3)

_Brave Bunnies_ streamed on the [Sunflower TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunflower_TV "Sunflower TV") YouTube channel, which launched in July 2022 and allowed [Ukrainian refugees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukrainian_refugee_crisis "Ukrainian refugee crisis") across Europe and the UK to watch ad-free children's programming in the Ukrainian language.[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-MchughSunflower-22)[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-EvansSunflower-23) Content was approved by a panel of media professionals, child psychologists and Ukrainian mothers. The creators of _Brave Bunnies_ along with partner companies waived their rights to enable the project.[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-MchughSunflower-22)[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-EvansSunflower-23)

It is broadcast on WildBrain's [Family Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Family_Jr. "Family Jr.") channel in Canada[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-BrzoznowskiWildbrain-24)[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-BabieraWildbrain-25) and on the Comcast WildBrain+ [SVOD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_on_demand#Subscription_models "Video on demand") channel in the United States.[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-SenalWildbrain-18) The second season was released in Canada in June 2023[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-TownsendWildbrain-21) followed by other territories later that year.[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-TodoWildbrain-26)

_Brave Bunnies_ was among the top-rated children's programs in Ukraine, the UK, Israel and Australia.[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-TyutyunenkoInterview-10) _[The New Voice of Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_Voice_of_Ukraine "The New Voice of Ukraine")_ applauded its message of diversity and acceptance.[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-NVfacts-14) A 2020 focus group by British research agency Childwise found that 79% of children aged 3 to 5 felt happier after watching the series, and 90% liked the characters.[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-NVfacts-14)

Books and merchandising
-----------------------

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Brave_Bunnies&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Books and merchandising")\]

Glowberry first distributed its books through the company's tablet app.[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-FilmUA-9) Following the launch of the TV series, various publishers were licensed to print physical books for _Brave Bunnies_, beginning with Italian-language editions by [Planeta Libre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De_Agostini "De Agostini")[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-UkrinformItaly-16)[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-WildbrainPrimary3-5) in 2021.[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-NVfacts-14) English-language editions were published by [Penguin Random House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penguin_Random_House "Penguin Random House") imprint Ladybird Books. These children's books include picture books ([board books](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Board_book "Board book")), [colouring books](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coloring_book "Coloring book"), [activity books](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Activity_book "Activity book"), and sticker books.[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-NVfacts-14)[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-TyutyunenkoInterview-10)

Canadian multinational toy company [Spin Master](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spin_Master "Spin Master") created a line of toys for the franchise.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-MilliganWildBrain-3)[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-YossmanWildbrain-11) The toy line includes figures, playsets, games, and plushies.[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_Bunnies#cite_note-Toybook-27)

2.content:
A 'Bunny' new series hit UK TV screens on Saturday 6th February 2021 at 9am on Milkshake-Channel 5. The international ensemble of the Ukrainian production company Glowberry, Spanish studio Anima and British distribution company Aardman have produced the wonderful pre-school animation Brave Bunnies. The series has already been a hit within the MIPJunior screenings library being one of the most viewed programmes with positive reviews amongst the most influential international experts.

This 2D series, created by Olga Cherepanova and directed by Tim Fehrenbach, follows a curious family of bunnies travelling on the Bunny Bus. Brother and sister Bunnies Bop and Boo discover a variety of different animals on their journey, often creating games and always making friends. Brave Bunnies explores the diversity within the world whilst encouraging young viewers to accept and embrace the differences in one another.

Fitzrovia Post provided its services to record all the voices for the series. The studio is well known for its dedication to provide impeccable audio for various animated projects. Glowberry and Fitzrovia Post have worked closely to cast the wonderfully talented voices heard in the series. Many of the characters were played by young children from as young at 5. The team at Fitzrovia are incredibly experienced in working with children; the studios hold a fun and safe atmosphere where their needs come first. The audio post production company has a reputation for specialising in children’s animation so this was bound to be the perfect partnership.

Voice records were directly impacted by the pandemic and as a result production slowed. However, Fitzrovia Post's director Keiran Brown, along with his team, invested in specialised technology and adapted to continue recording sessions with key characters remotely in a Covid-safe way. Without his leadership and ability to adapt the productions would have grounded to a halt. Fitzrovia Post has used this same approach to keep many productions afloat during this time.

“It was imperative that we continued recording with artists from the \[Brave Bunnies\] series to provide some sense of fun and normality to the children’s lives," said Keiran Brown.

This inspiring series has already seen deals for its broadcast with Nick Jr (UK), Super RTL (Germany), ABC (Australia), YLE (Finland), HOP! (Israel), PlusPlus (Ukraine), Daekyo (South Korea) and Milkshake! (UK). The international nature of the series alongside the lessons portrayed within the series are bound to see the series become a global success. This ambitious goal, when achieved, will see young audiences around the world grow up with the teachings shared is the beautifully illustrated production. Brave Bunnies will shape future generations with notions of acceptance and courageousness.

**Ukraine, Kyiv – October 22, 2020 – [BRAVE BUNNIES](https://bravebunnies.com/) animated series, based on the creative idea of the [Glowberry](https://glowberry.com.ua/) Ukrainian production, even before the official premiere on the world's TV channels have already received positive reviews from the most influential international experts and became one of the projects receiving most viewed programmes in the [MIPJunior](https://www.mipjunior.com/en-gb/what-is-mipjunior.html) screenings library.**

‘We are incredibly happy that BRAVE BUNNIES have managed to attract so much attention from the MIPJunior participants, since their expertise is of great importance to us and proves that we are moving in the right direction and are indeed creating the content of international level. As for now, we have quit an ambitious plan, which is gradually being implemented – to captivate the hearts of an audience of at least fifty, and better even a hundred countries of the world. Ukrainian kids will be among the first in the world to watch the adventures of Brave Bunnies on their TV screens. We plan that the premiere of the first 26 episodes will take place at the end of 2020 on the PLUSPLUS TV Channel. By March 2021, children of Italy, Germany, Finland, Israel, Great Britain will see the animated series as well. And this is definitely no final point for us’ comments [Olga Cherepanova](https://www.facebook.com/olga.cherepanova.5), the author of the idea and creative producer at Glowberry.

**Alison Taylor, Director of Distribution and Business Development at Aardman** says: “We were delighted to see Brave Bunnies feature in the top screening figures at MIPJunior, and to hear first-hand from buyers about what they love about the series during our meetings at Mipcom Online+. From the discussions had at the market, we’re confident that we will soon be in a position to announce further partnerships on the brand, in addition to the excellent broadcaster partners already announced.”

**Ángel Molinero, CEO (Spain) at Ánima** concluded: “Brave Bunnies is such a great show, the amazing performance it had during MipJunior proves it. We are honoured to be part of such a unique show and eager to introduce the Bunny family to kids all around the world.”

The success of BRAVE BUNNIES Series lies in the professional approach not only to the development of ideas, visual presentation and animation, but also to the involvement of child psychologists in the process of creating the original scripts. The series will be of great use for kids since it is aimed at developing empathy, acceptance and respect for diversity in our world.

The animated series is being produced in co-partnership with the [Ánima](https://helloanima.com/) Studio (Spain). Multi-award-winning animation studio [Aardman Animations](https://www.aardman.com/) (United Kingdom) is engaged in the global promotion of the first season of the animated series on the international market and has already confirmed the broadcast on seven TV channels around the world.

[Glowberry](https://glowberry.com.ua/) is a Ukrainian creative production that develops high-quality content 360° for Kids and families worldwide, founded in 2009 as a publishing house. Today, Glowberry focuses on a big international brand – [BRAVE BUNNIES](https://bravebunnies.com/). We develop it in a multitude of formats: animated TV-series for preschool kids, a line of original digital content, a series of books, and a line of licensed products for children.

[BRAVE BUNNIES](https://bravebunnies.com/) (52х7) is the 2D animated TV series follows the adventures of the Brave Bunnies Family, on their exciting Big Journey to explore the wider world around where they discover diverse new friends. The author of the original idea is [Olga Cherepanova](https://www.facebook.com/olga.cherepanova.5) (Ukraine). The Director is [\- Tim Fehrenbach](https://www.linkedin.com/in/timfehrenbach/) (Great Britain), the Head Writer for the series is [John van Bruggen](https://www.linkedin.com/in/john-van-bruggen-5980bb74/) (Canada) and the Art Director is – [Anna Sarvira](https://www.facebook.com/anna.sarvira.1) (Ukraine).

Amongst the partners of the project are such leaders of the international markets as animation studio [Ánima](https://helloanima.com/) (Spain), [Aardman](https://www.aardman.com/) [Animations](https://www.aardman.com/) (UK), [Big Picture Licensing](https://www.bigpicturelicensing.com/) (UK)[,](https://www.panaderia.xyz/) [La Panaderia Licensing & Marketing](https://www.panaderia.xyz/) (Mexico), [De Agostini Editore](https://www.deagostini.com/it/) (Italy), [Ladybird Books](https://www.ladybirdeducation.co.uk/) [Limited](https://www.ladybirdeducation.co.uk/) (UK), [FILM UA Group](https://film.ua/uk/) (Ukraine), and many others soon to follow.

[MIPJunior](https://www.mipjunior.com/) is the World's Leading Kids Entertainment Industry Event. It gathers the most influential buyers, commissioners, producers, development executives and distributors from the global Kids TV industry. **MIPJunior** is the largest international digital screenings venue for kids content, with 600+ buyers attending to screen 1,300 kids programmes, projects and IPs.

[Aardman Animations](https://www.aardman.com/) is the global content distributor for the first season of the [BRAVE BUNNIES](https://bravebunnies.com/) series. It is an independent animation studio based in Bristol (UK) founded in 1976. Amongst its awards are BAFTA, Oscar, and Gold Cannes Lions. The studio produces feature films, series, advertisements, games, and interactive entertainment. Its console game [11-11: Memories Retold](https://www.aardman.com/work/11-11-memories-retold-game/) was nominated for BAFTA, and its [StorySign](https://www.aardman.com/blog/creating-storysign-app-for-deaf-readers/) app won four Gold Cannes Lions. The popularity of Aardman brands, like Wallace & Gromit, Shaun the Sheep, and Morph, places the company amongst the leaders in the production of quality visual content for cinema, TV, and digital platforms.

[Ánima](https://helloanima.com/) is a leading family entertainment company based in Mexico City, Madrid, and the Canary Islands. It specializes in 2D and CGI animation. The studio creates, produces, and manages high-quality entertainment brands and develops original projects for kids and the whole family. Ánima became the first studio in the world to work with a Warner Bros’ IP, producing a hugely successful film: Top Cat, the Movie, which had a rousing success in the British box-office. Ánima created many successful projects like Space Chickens in Space with Disney and Cake Entertainment, Legend Quest and Legend Quest Masters of Myth with Netflix. As a service studio, it worked with Nickelodeon, Cartoon Network, and Illumination Entertainment.

Using the example of Brave Bunnies and their friends, parents can explain how to interact with other kids in the kindergarten or at the playground. In each episode, Brave Bunnies meet friends and come up with a fun game to play together.

On October 21 a new publication for the youngest children, _Brave__Bunnies__in__the__Jungle__,_ will see the world and become the initial book of the series about bunnies’ adventures. You can become one of the first book owners and talk to its authors on October 20, at 11 AM in  [Zelenka](https://www.facebook.com/coworkingzelenka/) Coworking with Children (11/1 Yaroslaviv Val). Come by yourself or take your kids with you!

_Brave_ _Bunnies_ _in_ _the__J ungle_is not just a book but an adventure and a game where courageous and inquisitive bunnies ardently get to know the unfamiliar world around them. They set out on journeys and find new friends on every page. This book is designed to develop children’s imagination and to understand the diversity of our world.

![Image 1](https://film.ua/uploads/assets/images/photo_2018-10-18_16-45-11.jpg)

The author of bunny idea and creative concept of bunny world is [Olga](https://www.facebook.com/olga.cherepanova.5) Cherepanova, author of many children’s books and producer of animated projects. The artist for the bunny world was Anna Sarvira, a recipient of international awards and illustrator of over 20 children’s publications. [Natalia](https://www.facebook.com/profile.php?id=100001067773800) Pashko, practical psychologist at Municipal Center for Children, helped to make the material as useful and accessible for the youngsters as possible.

![Image 2](https://film.ua/uploads/assets/images/%D0%90%D0%BD%D0%BD%D0%B0%20%D0%A1%D0%B0%D1%80%D0%B2%D0%B8%D1%80%D0%B0.png)

_“Understandable characters, the format of adventures and also the joint ritual play help the children develop empathy, accept others and learn something new. A meeting with each character is a new experience of communication and a new emotion. The book about Brave Bunnies can become a great family tradition of joint reading. It will also serve as a clue for parents telling them how to talk to children about the world’s diversity, the differences of others, the significance of various feelings and considerate treatment of one another,”_ says Natalia Pashko, child psychologist, sharing her thoughts about the book.

The extraordinary game book was created based on an animated serious for preschoolers, _Brave__Bunnies__._Glowberry creative production is the idea author and the developer of Brave Bunnies universe: TV show, series of books, souvenirs, mobile apps, etc. Now the animated series is in development stage but already attracts attention of professional media community. This autumn the project became a finalist at the pitching of a major TV animation festival Cartoon Forum and received a lot of positive feedback from the representatives of leading global TV channels.

_“__The_ _concept__,_ _the_ _visuals__,_ _the_ _script__,_ _and_ _the market potential are excellent. It is intriguing to find out the result. I want to see more!” said Sarah Muller, Vice President of Children’s and Youth Programming at_ _Sony Pictures__._

_“__I_ _really_ _liked_ _the_ _design_ _of_ _Bunnies_ _characters_ _and_ _world_ _and_ _also_ _cute_ _children__’__s_ _humor_ _and_ _the_ _global_ _goal__,”_ _notes_ _Henrietta_ _Hurford__\-__Jones__,_ _director_ _of_ _children__’__s_ _content_ _at_ _BBC_ _Studios__._

You can get a taste of book characters from the teaser:

Just a reminder: the book’s official presentation will take place on October 20, at 11 AM in Zelenka Coworking with Children at 11/1 Yaroslaviv Val.

To find out how to buy _Brave__Bunnies__in__the__Jungle_and also other publications from Glowberry, go to our resources:

[http://glowberry.com.ua/](http://glowberry.com.ua/)

[https://www.facebook.com/glowberry.com.ua/](https://www.facebook.com/glowberry.com.ua/)

[https://www.instagram.com/glowberry.com.ua/](https://www.instagram.com/glowberry.com.ua/)

**_FYI_****_:_** _Glowberry_ _is__a__creative__production__studio__founded__in_ _2009_ _and__producing__multimedia__content__for__children__._ _In nine years of its functioning, Glowberry published over 30 printed books and interactive apps for kids played and read in more than 25 countries of the world._

_In_ _2016_ _the__company__became__part__of_ [_FILM.UA Group_](https://film.ua/)_,_ _the__biggest__media__holding__in__Eastern__Europe__,_ _and__started__developing__a__range__of__animated__series__for__children__based__on its successful projects. They include_ Mom Hurries Home _and_ Brave Bunnies_._

[_Cartoon Forum_](http://www.cartoon-media.eu/cartoon-forum)_is__a__TV__animation__festival__held__since_ _1990._ _This year, the forum took place on September 10-13 in Toulouse and was visited by almost a thousand participants: broadcasters, investors and potential partners from more than 40 countries._

Glowberry Creative Production. We create fun, exciting content for kids and families worldwide.

Our company was originally established in 2009, in Ukraine, as a niche publishing house, focusing on discovering new talent in kids' literature and illustration. Today Glowberry is a dynamic creative and production company with a large, international team creating children’s animated content and brands that we distribute and license all around the world. Our creative team specializes in high-quality children’s content for global audiences, while the distribution and licensing teams work with exceptional partners to promote our content all over the world. Our partners are world leaders in animation, broadcasting, film production and licensing. We believe that creativity, openness to diversity in the world and the ability to celebrate those things and bring positivity and joy makes children’s lives exciting and we are guided by these ideas in our work. We are extremely proud of the entire and growing team of excellent artists and professionals from multiple fields across the world who are now engaged to work on Glowberry products.

WildBrain, Glowberry and Ánima partner for Brave Bunnies
========================================================

Posted by [Rebecca Ash](https://www.totallicensing.com/author/rebecca-ash/ "Posts by Rebecca Ash") | Dec 2, 2022 | [News](https://www.totallicensing.com/category/news/) |

![Image 15: WildBrain, Glowberry and Ánima partner for Brave Bunnies](https://www.totallicensing.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/BBF_Moose_and_Bunnies-1280x640.jpg)

WildBrain has partnered with Ukrainian kids’ producer Glowberry to bring the beloved Brave Bunnies preschool brand into its portfolio of kids’ and family franchises. Under the arrangement, WildBrain has assured the continuation of the popular _Brave Bunnies_ series which was disrupted by the Russian invasion of Ukraine. Working together with Glowberry and the leading Ibero-American animation studio, Ánima, WildBrain will now lead the global management of Brave Bunnies, leveraging its 360° capabilities across production, distribution and consumer products. Brave Bunnies was created by Olga Cherepanova, co-founder of Glowberry and Creative Producer on the series.

WildBrain’s Vancouver animation studio will be co-producing season two of the _Brave Bunnies_ series with Glowberry and Ánima, producers of season one. Delivery of season two is expected beginning in June 2023. WildBrain will also handle global distribution of all _Brave Bunnies_ content, while its dedicated consumer products agency, WildBrain CPLG, will manage licensing and merchandising worldwide. WildBrain’s own Family Jr. channel has picked up _Brave Bunnies_ season one for exclusive linear telecast in Canada. Glowberry retains distribution and licensing rights for the brand in Ukraine, while Ánima retains distribution rights in Spain. The three-way partnership, which was facilitated by Big Picture Licensing, sees WildBrain become majority stakeholder in the Brave Bunnies IP, with Glowberry and Ánima as minority stakeholders.

Eric Ellenbogen, CEO of WildBrain, said: “Brave Bunnies is a kids’ property born of tremendous creative vision and has the potential to be a major preschool franchise, having already established a solid foundation with audiences through compelling content and consumer products. Following the terrible events in Ukraine this year, we saw it as vital to ensure the future of this wonderful property, and we couldn’t be more pleased now to be collaborating with Olga Cherepanova and her Glowberry team, along with the creative team at Ánima, on the next big adventures for the Brave Bunnies.”

_Brave Bunnies_ is a 2D-animated series for kids aged 2-5, which follows the adventures of two curious and inspiring bunny siblings—Boo and Bop—who create joy and excitement in their lives by bravely seeking out new friends, games and experiences. Fostering values of curiosity, creativity, eagerness, openness and responsibility, the series encourages kids to ask the question “What if…?” as they embrace new experiences with “bunny bravery” to learn and grow.

Cherepanova said: “I created Brave Bunnies to help children all over the world communicate with different friends without any fears or stereotypes, respecting the diversity of our world. Each episode of Brave Bunnies shows real-life examples of how to find a unique approach to each person without pressure or changing anyone’s uniqueness. This idea is essential for healthy childhood development.

“Unfortunately, after the Russian invasion of Ukraine, the Glowberry team faced significant challenges. Many employees were forced to flee Kyiv because of personal safety and the lives of their loved ones. But thanks to the support of partners like WildBrain and Ánima, now we have the opportunity to continue to create and share Brave Bunnies together.

“Glowberry is glad to have WildBrain as a partner on board. When such a prominent company lends a hand for a smaller one, especially in a situation as complex as ours, it boosts a project immediately. Brave Bunnies is an international project, aired in many countries, so the partnership with WildBrain is a logical and necessary step in our development.

“I’m proud and happy that this project born in Ukraine will now continue to spread around the world helping the next generation develop respect for diversity and build relationships based on co-creation and cooperation rather than on fear and violence. On behalf of the Ukrainian team, I want to express my deep gratitude to all the partners and talented people working together on Brave Bunnies, who have done so much despite the challenges we all faced. We do hope for peace in Ukraine and will do everything possible for a peaceful tomorrow.”

Ángel Molinero, CEO Spain at Ánima, added: “From Ánima we want to thank both WildBrain and Glowberry. We are very excited about the future of the project and we believe WildBrain is the perfect partner to give continuity to the Brave Bunnies brand.”

DeAgostini publishing imprint Planeta Libri launch Brave Bunnies books in Italy.
================================================================================

by [BPL admin](https://bigpicturelicensing.com/news/author/dan_mtdwx4527/ "Posts by BPL admin") | May 16, 2022

First ever Brave Bunnies launched in Italy with our strategic partner for the territory DeAgostini and their publishing imprint Planeta Libri to rollout 10 new titles in year 1.

The books based on the Ukrainian kids’ series BRAVE BUNNIES are out in Italy  
The sales of the first collection of books published by DeAgostini opened this Autumn.  
  
From now on, the characters of the BRAVE BUNNIES series have become even closer to their little fans. Italian publisher DeA Planeta Libri, which is a subsidiary of Grupo Planeta and DeAgostini became the first company to publish books based on the popular kids’ series. The deal was arranged by KidsMe, the distributor and agent for BRAVE BUNNIES in Italy. As of Q4 2021, the first books about the adventures of the Brave Bunnies appeared on the shelves of Italian bookstores. The book collection includes sticker books Amici Incredibili (Incredible Friends) and In Giro per il Mondo (Around the World),  
as well as hardcover books Eroi Controvento (Brave Heroes), Strisce da Esploratore (Hidden Treasure), and Pulizia Cosmica  
(A Great Mess). In October DeA Planeta Libri launched the books in leading book chains with 800 stores nationwide, as well as on online platforms. Besides the book chains, the books are available in over 300 mass-market outlets across Italy.  
**Olga Cherepanova, author and Creative producer of BRAVE BUNNIES,** comments:  
“The first release of books based on BRAVE BUNNIES is a major event for the team of the series. This release is another step  
toward building a full-fledged universe around the BRAVE BUNNIES series and its characters. Each new viewer of the series is motivating and inspiring us to go forward. That’s why we are always excited to gain new fans and connect with the established fanbase in a new way — through print media. We are proud to work with the talented team of KidsMe and DeA Planeta Libri — the undisputed market leader.” KidsMe became Glowberry’s first partners and paved the way for the global distribution of the project.  
**Brenda Maffuchi, Chief of Co-Productions, Licensing and Sales Officer at DeAgostini/KidsMe** said: “We are very happy to have confirmed this first license for BRAVE BUNNIES in Italy. It will be the first of many licenses and contracts we are working on in the Italian market. We are hoping to confirm these agreements very soon because we know that BRAVE BUNNIES is an IP with great potential and we can’t wait to see the Brand’s products in the Italian market.”  
In Italy, BRAVE BUNNIES premiered this spring on RAIYoYo. The series first aired on the streaming service Rai Play and began airing on Rai YoYo nationwide on April 19.

BRAVE BUNNIES is a unique entertainment and educational series for preschool kids, based on the original story by creative producer Olga Cherepanova, created in coproduction with a Spanish animation studio Ánima. The visual style of the series is created by a famous Ukrainian illustrator Anna Sarvira. The Director of the series is Tim Fehrenbach (UK). The Head Writer for the series is John van Bruggen (Canada). Aardman Animations, the Oscar-winning animation studio, is the international distributor of the series. Before the world premiere, BRAVE BUNNIES became the pitch finalist of the international animation festival Cartoon Forum 2018. The project was created with the support of FILM.UA Group, the State Film Agency, and the Ministry of Youth and Sports of Ukraine.

WildBrain acquires _Brave Bunnies_ from Glowberry in Ukraine
============================================================

##### The Canadian studio will co-produce season two, as well as spearheading global distribution and brand management.

By [Ryan Tuchow](https://kidscreen.com/author/rtuchow/ "Posts by Ryan Tuchow")

December 1, 2022

WildBrain has acquired Ukrainian success story _Brave Bunnies_, a 2D-animated preschool series that currently airs in more than 80 territories around the world.

Coming on board as a co-producer for season two, WildBrain will air the show in Canada on its Family Jr. linear net. And the company’s CPLG team has also taken on worldwide licensing and merchandising for the IP.

Brave Bunnies revolves around two rabbits who explore the world, play games and meet new animal friends, with a focus on encouraging creativity, openness and bravery. It was created by Glowberry co-founder Olga Cherepanova, who serves as the show’s creative producer. Season one (52 x seven minutes) was a co-pro between Glowberry and Spain’s Ánima Estudios, which retain distribution and CP rights in their domestic regions. But this new deal makes WildBrain a majority stakeholder in the IP.

Broadcasters including [WarnerMedia](https://kidscreen.com/2022/04/01/deals-of-the-week-41-entertainment-glowberry-one-animation/) (international), ABC Australia and Milkshake! (UK) picked up the first season of _Brave Bunnies_, which premiered in February 2021. [Spin Master](https://kidscreen.com/2021/11/22/spin-master-hops-onto-shelves-with-brave-bunnies/) hopped on board as global master toy partner last year and launched a first range of products this spring.

_Brave Bunnies_ has “the potential to be a major preschool franchise,” said WildBrain CEO Eric Ellenbogen in a release. With its existing broadcast and consumer products deals, it has a solid base to build upon, he added.

Before Russia invaded Ukraine this February, Glowberry was already underway on producing season two. [The incursion halted that work,](https://kidscreen.com/2022/03/21/ukrainian-kids-content-producers-fear-for-industrys-future/) and forced the studio’s staff to flee the country.

WildBrain has set a June 2023 delivery date for season two (also 52 x seven minutes), and its Vancouver studio will join Glowberry and Anima on the production.
